entries.answer:
For this exact job, I would pick **Wan 2.7** first if 4K is a hard requirement, because it is the only one of the four where the sources I found explicitly mention up to 4K output while also supporting instruction-based video editing and motion-preserving edits.[1][2][3]
If iterative, chat-like refinement matters more than output resolution, Gemini Omni Flash is the strongest editing workflow on paper, but its uploaded-video editing has regional limits in the EEA, which matters for a user in Hungary.[4]

## Task fit

Your edit is a very specific pose-and-contact change: you want the white-haired boy repositioned so he is gently snuggled against the brown-haired boy’s shoulder, while everything else stays stable and photorealistic. Models that do best here are the ones that explicitly support instruction-based editing, preservation of the original motion or scene structure, and reference guidance for identity consistency.[5][6][2][4]

Gemini Omni Flash is especially strong for this kind of surgical change because Google describes it as conversational video editing that preserves the parts you do not mention, and its prompt guide explicitly recommends simple edits plus the phrase “Keep everything else the same.”[4]
Wan 2.7 is the better overall pick for your stated target because it supports natural-language video editing, preserves original motion and structure, accepts multi-image guidance, and is explicitly advertised at up to 4K resolution.[7][2][3]

## Ranking

| Model | How it fits this edit | Main drawback |
|---|---|---|
| Wan 2.7 Video Edit | Best match if you want the final result to be ultra-realistic and as close to true 4K delivery as possible, while still editing an existing clip with natural language and preserving motion structure. [2][3][1] | I found strong capability claims, but less official prompt guidance than Gemini for conversational turn-by-turn refinement. [8][2][4] |
| Gemini Omni Flash Video Edit | Best match if you want to iterate repeatedly on subtle body positioning, because it supports conversational editing, stateful follow-up edits, subject references, and instructions that preserve everything else. [4][9] | Google says editing uploaded videos is not currently available in the EEA, Switzerland, and the UK, and it also restricts editing uploads containing minors in those regions. [4] |
| Seedance 2.0 Video Edit | Strong middle option if you need many references, because sources describe it as reference-friendly, realistic, and able to edit uploaded footage while accepting up to 12 mixed assets. [10][5][11] | The sources I found position it more as a strong general generation/reference model, and they mention 1080p rather than explicit 4K for this workflow. [10][11] |
| HappyHorse 1.0 Video Edit | Usable for prompt-driven edits with optional reference images and predictable workflow, especially if you want a cheaper, simpler pass. [6] | It tops out at 720p or 1080p, so it is the weakest fit for an “ultra-realistic 4K” requirement. [6] |

## Best choice

If your brief stays exactly the same, Wan 2.7 is the safest first choice because the request combines two hard things at once: a delicate relational pose edit and an explicit 4K realism target.[2][3]
Gemini Omni Flash would be my first choice only in a workflow where you expect to do several follow-up edits like “closer,” “more natural cheek angle,” or “keep the hair exactly the same,” because its official documentation is the clearest on iterative editing and preservation.[4]

Seedance 2.0 sits in the middle because it appears strong for reference-guided realism and footage editing, but the material I found does not give it the same clear edge as Wan on 4K output or as Gemini on conversational editing behavior.[10][5][4]
HappyHorse 1.0 is the weakest option for this task simply because its published edit workflow is capped at 1080p, which conflicts with your stated target before quality is even judged.[6]

## Prompting

For this kind of edit, shorter and more surgical wording is likely better than a long cinematic paragraph, because Gemini’s editing guide explicitly recommends simple prompts for edits and says to add “Keep everything else the same” when you want consistency.[4]
A good base version would be: “Move the white-haired boy so he is gently snuggled against the brown-haired boy’s shoulder. Preserve both faces, hair, clothing, camera angle, lighting, and background. Keep everything else the same. Ultra-realistic, natural skin texture, 4K finish.”[4]

If you have reference stills of both boys from the source clip, Wan, Seedance, and HappyHorse all benefit from reference guidance for identity or appearance consistency, and Gemini also supports subject references in addition to edit prompts.[11][7][6][4]
